title: Definitions and interpretation - invention
summary: "invention" means a new product or process involving an inventive step and capable of industrial application.
notes: Fundamental definition establishing criteria for patentability.

title: Definitions and interpretation - inventive step
summary: "inventive step" means a feature of an invention that involves technical advance as compared to the existing knowledge or having economic significance or both and that makes the invention not obvious to a person skilled in the art.
notes: Critical for fighting patent applications that merely combine traditional knowledge.

title: What are not inventions - contrary to public order/morality
summary: An invention, the primary or intended use or commercial exploitation of which could be contrary to public order or morality or which causes serious prejudice to human, animal or plant life or health or to the environment.
notes: Used to protect plant life and environment.

title: What are not inventions - discovery of living thing or non-living substance
summary: The mere discovery of a scientific principle or the formulation of an abstract theory or discovery of any living thing or non-living substance occurring in nature.
notes: Directly prevents the patenting of naturally occurring medicinal plants and minerals.

title: What are not inventions - mere discovery of a new form of known substance
summary: The mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy of that substance or the mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance or of the mere use of a known process, machine or apparatus unless such known process results in a new product or employs at least one new reactant.
notes: Prevents patenting of new forms (like extracts) of known Ayurvedic substances unless significant efficacy enhancement is proven.

title: What are not inventions - mere admixture
summary: A substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance.
notes: Highly relevant for traditional Ayurvedic polyherbal formulations.

title: What are not inventions - traditional knowledge
summary: An invention which in effect, is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components.
notes: The most critical section for TKDL integration. Expressly prohibits patenting of TK.

title: Contents of specifications - disclosure of biological material
topic: disclosure of source/geographical origin, biological material
summary: If the applicant mentions a biological material in the specification which may not be described in such a way as to satisfy clauses (a) and (b), and if such material is not available to the public, the application shall be completed by depositing the material... and disclose the source and geographical origin of the biological material in the specification, when used in an invention.
notes: Mandates disclosure of source/origin of Indian biological resources used in inventions.

title: Request for examination
summary: No application for a patent shall be examined unless the applicant or any other interested person makes a request in the prescribed manner within the prescribed period.
notes: Procedural context for patent processing.

title: Opposition to the patent (Pre-grant) - non-disclosure of biological material
topic: opposition, biological material, disclosure of source/geographical origin
summary: Pre-grant opposition ground: that the complete specification does not disclose or wrongly mentions the source or geographical origin of biological material used for the invention.
notes: Enables third parties to oppose patents that fail to disclose or falsely claim source of biological material.

title: Opposition to the patent (Pre-grant) - anticipation by traditional knowledge
summary: Pre-grant opposition ground: that the invention so far as claimed in any claim of the complete specification is anticipated having regard to the knowledge, oral or otherwise, available within any local or indigenous community in India or elsewhere.
notes: The primary mechanism used in conjunction with TKDL to oppose bad patents prior to grant.

title: Opposition to the patent (Post-grant) - non-disclosure of biological material
topic: opposition, biological material, disclosure of source/geographical origin
summary: Post-grant opposition ground (within one year): that the complete specification does not disclose or wrongly mentions the source or geographical origin of biological material used for the invention.
notes: Allows challenging a granted patent for biological material source failure.

title: Opposition to the patent (Post-grant) - anticipation by traditional knowledge
summary: Post-grant opposition ground (within one year): that the invention so far as claimed in any claim of the complete specification is anticipated having regard to the knowledge, oral or otherwise, available within any local or indigenous community in India or elsewhere.
notes: Allows challenging a granted patent based on traditional knowledge.

title: Revocation of patents - non-disclosure of biological material
topic: revocation, biological material, disclosure of source/geographical origin
summary: Ground for revocation: that the complete specification does not disclose or wrongly mentions the source or geographical origin of biological material used for the invention.
notes: Allows revocation of a patent at any time during its term on this ground.

title: Revocation of patents - anticipation by traditional knowledge
summary: Ground for revocation: that the invention so far as claimed in any claim of the complete specification was anticipated having regard to the knowledge, oral or otherwise, available within any local or indigenous community in India or elsewhere.
notes: Allows revocation of a patent at any time during its term based on traditional knowledge.

title: Compulsory licences
summary: Any person interested may make an application to the Controller for grant of compulsory licence on patent after three years from date of grant of a patent on grounds including reasonable requirements of public not satisfied, or invention is not available to public at reasonably affordable price, or invention is not worked in the territory of India.
notes: Can be utilized if patented medicinal products derived from TK are not accessible to the public.

title: Supplementary provisions as to convention applications
summary: Provisions detailing the requirements for convention applications, including the furnishing of copies of specifications filed in convention countries and translations if not in English.
notes: Relevant for tracking international filings that may misappropriate traditional knowledge.

title: International applications designating or electing India
summary: Details the procedures and timelines for entering the national phase in India for an international application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT).
notes: Critical for opposing PCT applications entering India.

title: Opposition to the patent (Pre-grant)
summary: Procedure for pre-grant opposition under section 25(1). Representation for opposition must be filed at the appropriate office with a statement and evidence.
notes: Governs the actual process CSIR/TKDL would use to submit evidence against an application.

title: Filing of notice of opposition (Post-grant)
summary: The procedure for filing a notice of opposition to a granted patent under section 25(2), to be made in Form 7 and sent to the Controller in duplicate.
notes: Procedural rule for submitting a post-grant opposition.
